name: St. Jude
bio:
Jude, also called Thaddaeus, was one of the twelve apostles, listed in the Gospels of Luke and John and in the Acts of the Apostles. He is traditionally identified as the author of the short New Testament epistle that bears his name, which urges believers to persevere in faith amid false teachers.

According to tradition, Jude preached the gospel in Judea, Samaria, Syria, and Mesopotamia, and was martyred in Persia around 65 AD, often depicted with a club or axe. He is sometimes confused with Judas Iscariot, which may explain why devotion to him developed slowly.

Because his name was so easily mistaken for that of the traitor, the faithful came to regard him as the saint of last resort, and he is now invoked worldwide as the patron of impossible causes and desperate situations.
